assets.alt: Separate a variant’s origin, inheritance and later selection
assets.caption: Separate a variant’s origin, inheritance and later selection.
assets.equivalentExplanation: A somatic mutation can pass to daughter cells by mitosis but, when confined to that body-cell lineage, usually does not enter offspring through the germ line. A mutation in cells contributing to gametes may be inherited depending on which gamete contributes. Mutation creates new sequence variation; meiotic recombination primarily reshuffles existing variants. Neither origin nor inheritance proves a variant will increase in frequency: later reproductive contribution and environmental conditions matter. Mutations are not directed toward an organism’s anticipated need. Harmful,neutral or beneficial effects require a stated context and evidence across molecular,cellular and broader outcomes.
